questions.question: Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kinetic energy**__.

__
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• All particles of matter are in constant motion, and this motion is a result of their kinetic energy.
 
• The temperature of a substance is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
• Increased kinetic energy results in faster movement of particles, which can lead to changes in the state of matter (e.g., from solid to liquid).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is a form of energy that an object or a particle has by reason of its motion.
 
• It is defined as the work needed to accelerate a body of a given mass from rest to its stated velocity.
 
• Once the object reaches this velocity, it maintains its kinetic energy unless its speed changes.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy (KE) is given by KE = 1/2 mv², where m is the mass and v is the velocity.
 
 
 
• **Other Forms of Energy:**
 
 
• **Nuclear Energy:** Energy released during nuclear fission or fusion, especially when used to generate electricity.
 
• **Chemical Energy:** Energy stored in the bonds of chemical compounds, released in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Mechanical Energy:** The sum of kinetic and potential energy in an object that is used to do work.
 
 
 
• **State of Matter:**
 
 
• Solid: Particles are closely packed and only vibrate in place.
 
• Liquid: Particles are close together but can move/slide past one another.
 
• Gas: Particles are far apart and move freely.
 
• Plasma: A state of matter similar to gas, but the particles are electrically charged.
 
 
 
• **Temperature and Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance.
 
• Higher temperatures correspond to higher average kinetic energies.
 
• As the temperature increases, the particles move faster, and thus the kinetic energy increases.

questions.question: The work done by the motor per unit time is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which **work is done** or energy is transferred in a system.
 
• In mathematical terms, **Power = Work Done / Time Taken**.
 
• Its **SI unit** is the **watt (W)**, where 1 watt is equal to 1 joule per second.
 
• In the context of a motor, power refers to the amount of **mechanical work** the motor performs per unit time.
 
• For example, if a motor lifts a load, its power can be measured by the force it applies and the speed at which it lifts the load.
 
• Electric motors are often rated in terms of their **power output**, expressed in watts, kilowatts, or horsepower.
 
• Power is a key parameter in understanding the efficiency and performance of machines and systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Energy**__

 __
 
• **Energy** is the capacity to do work or produce heat. It exists in various forms such as **kinetic energy, potential energy, thermal energy, and chemical energy**.
 
• Unlike power, which is a rate, energy is a measure of the total amount of work done or heat produced.
 
• The **SI unit of energy** is the **joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration**__
 __
 
• **Acceleration** refers to the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• The **SI unit** of acceleration is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
 
 
• **Momentum**__
 
 
• **Momentum** is the product of an object's **mass and velocity**.
 
• It is a vector quantity and is conserved in isolated systems, as per the law of conservation of momentum.
 
• The **SI unit** of momentum is **kilogram meter per second (kg·m/s)**.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg, which is moving with the constant velocity 5 m/sec, is ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**25 joules**__.

__
 
• The formula to calculate **kinetic energy** is given by: **K.E. = (1/2) * m * v²**, where **m** is the mass of the body and **v** is its velocity.
 
• In the given problem, the mass of the body (**m**) is **2 kg**, and the velocity (**v**) is **5 m/sec**.
 
• Substitute the values in the formula: **K.E. = (1/2) * 2 * (5)²**.
 
• On solving: **K.E. = (1) * 25 = 25 joules.**
 
• Thus, the **kinetic energy** of the body is **25 joules**.
 
• **Kinetic energy** is a form of energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
 
• It is directly proportional to the **mass** of the object and the square of its **velocity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• **Kinetic energy** is a scalar quantity and has no direction.
 
• It is measured in **joules (J)**, which is the SI unit of energy.
 
• Applications of kinetic energy include **power generation, vehicular motion, and industrial machinery.**
 
 
 
• **Mass**__

• **Mass** is a measure of the amount of matter in an object.
 
• It is measured in **kilograms (kg)** in the SI system.
 
• Mass is independent of gravity, unlike weight.

questions.question: A car moves with a uniform velocity (v) in a particular direction for a distance (s) under the action of a force (F) acting in the same direction. The work done by the force will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Work done (W) by a force (F) is calculated using the formula: **W = F × s**, where s is the displacement.
 
• In this problem, the force (F) and displacement (s) are in the same direction.
 
• Hence, the work done is positive and is given by the product of the force and displacement.
 
• Uniform velocity (v) indicates that the force is applied uniformly over the distance.
 
• Therefore, the correct option for the work done by the force is **Fs** (Option 2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force and Work**

 
 
• Force is a vector quantity that causes an object to move or change its motion.
 
• Work is a scalar quantity and is the measure of energy transfer when a force moves an object over a distance.
 
 
 
• **Energy**
 
 
• Energy is the capacity to do work and is measured in joules (J).
 
• Work and energy are closely related; the work done on an object transfers energy to the object.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy**
 
 
• An object moving with velocity (v) has kinetic energy given by the formula: KE = 0.5 × m × v².
 
• The work done by a force can change the kinetic energy of an object.

questions.question: If a man lifts 1 kg of load to the height of 2.5 m from the ground, then assuming acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/sec², magnitude of the work done by the man is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mass (m) = 1 kg

Height (h) = 2.5 m

Acceleration due to gravity (g) = 10 m/s²

**Concept:**

The work done by a force is given by the formula:

W = m × g × h

Where:

 
• W = Work done
 
• m = Mass of the object
 
• g = Acceleration due to gravity
 
• h = Height to which the object is lifted

 

**Calculation:**

⇒ W = 1 × 10 × 2.5

⇒ W = 25 joules

**∴ The magnitude of the work done by the man is 25 joules.**

questions.question: When the force and the displacement are in the same direction, then work done will be:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the **force** and **displacement** are in the same direction, the **angle between force and displacement** is **0 degrees**.
 
• The mathematical expression for **work done** is given as: **Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• When θ = 0°, the value of **cos(θ) = 1**, so the formula simplifies to: **W = F × d × 1 = F × d.**
 
• Since both force and displacement are in the same direction, their magnitudes are **positive**, leading to a **positive value for work done**.
 
• This signifies that the energy is being **transferred to the object**, causing displacement in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Examples include pushing a box forward or lifting an object upwards, where the displacement occurs in the same direction as the applied force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero**__

 __
 
• If the angle between force and displacement is **90 degrees**, then the **cos(90°) = 0**, resulting in **zero work done**.
 
• This happens when the force does not contribute to the displacement, such as carrying an object horizontally without vertical displacement.
 
 
 
• **Negative**__
 __
 
• If the force and displacement are in **opposite directions**, the angle θ = 180°, and **cos(180°) = -1**, leading to **negative work done**.
 
• Negative work is observed when a force opposes the motion, such as friction slowing down a moving object.
 
 
 
• **Either Positive or Negative**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the work done depends on the **specific relationship** between the force and displacement directions.
 
• It cannot be both positive and negative at the same time; it depends on the angle θ.

• Since cos(0°) is equal to **1**, the work done is calculated as: **Work = 10 × 2 × 1 = 20 joules**.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **kinetic energy** of a moving object is directly proportional to its **mass** and the **square of its velocity**.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is given as **KE = (1/2) mv²**, where:
 
 
• **m** represents the mass of the object.
 
• **v** represents the velocity of the object.
 
 
 
• This implies that an increase in either the **mass** or the **velocity** (with velocity having a greater impact due to being squared) will result in an increase in the **kinetic energy**.
 
• **Pressure** does not have a direct relationship with kinetic energy in this context. Pressure is defined as **force per unit area** and pertains to different physical phenomena.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is that the kinetic energy depends on **both the mass of the body** and the **square of its velocity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• The **mass** is a scalar quantity that represents the amount of matter contained in an object.
 
• It is measured in **kilograms (kg)** in the SI unit system.
 
• In the context of kinetic energy, the mass determines the proportion of energy for a given velocity.
 
 
 
• **Square of the velocity**__
 __
 
• The **velocity** of an object refers to its speed in a specific direction and is a vector quantity.
 
• Since the velocity is squared in the formula, it has a larger influence on the kinetic energy than the mass.
 
• For example, doubling the velocity of an object will quadruple its kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Pressure**__
 
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the force exerted per unit area and is measured in **Pascals (Pa)**.
 
• It is unrelated to the kinetic energy of a moving object in this context.
 
• Pressure is often studied in the context of fluids, gases, and thermodynamics.

questions.question: Which of the following quantities remains conserved for a system which is subjected to a conservative force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Total mechanical energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Total mechanical energy** (sum of kinetic and potential energy) remains conserved in a system subjected to a conservative force.
 
• In a conservative force field, the work done by the force only depends on the initial and final positions, not on the path taken.
 
• This conservation implies that any change in potential energy of the system is exactly balanced by a change in kinetic energy.
 
• Examples of conservative forces include gravitational force, electrostatic force, and spring force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conservative Force**

 
 
• A force is considered conservative if the work it does on a particle moving between two points is independent of the path taken.
 
• Examples include gravitational force, electrostatic force, and the elastic force in springs.
 
 
 
• **Mechanical Energy**
 
 
• Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic energy (energy due to motion) and potential energy (energy due to position).
 
• In the absence of non-conservative forces, the total mechanical energy of a system remains constant.
 
 
 
• **Non-Conservative Forces**
 
 
• Non-conservative forces, such as friction and air resistance, cause energy to be transferred out of the system, often as heat.
 
• These forces do not have the property of path independence.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conservation**
 
 
• Energy conservation is a fundamental principle stating that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
 
• In a closed system not subjected to external forces, the total energy remains constant.

__
 
• The work done to take a body of mass ‘m’ to a height ‘h’ is equal to the change in gravitational potential energy, which is calculated as **W = mgh**.
 
• Gravitational potential energy depends on the mass of the body (m), acceleration due to gravity (g), and the height (h) from the reference point.
 
• This formula assumes that the gravitational force is constant, which is a valid approximation near the Earth's surface.
 
• The correct option, **mgh**, signifies the direct proportionality of work done to mass and height when moving a body against gravity.
 
• This concept is widely used in physics to calculate energy transformations in systems involving gravitational forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:**

 
 
• It is the energy possessed by an object due to its position relative to Earth or another gravitational source.
 
• Formula: U = mgh, where ‘U’ is potential energy, ‘m’ is mass, ‘g’ is acceleration due to gravity, and ‘h’ is height.
 
 
 
• **Work Done Against Gravity:**
 
 
• Work is defined as the energy required to move a body against a force—in this case, gravitational force.
 
• The work done is calculated using W = Force × Distance, which simplifies to W = mgh for gravitational systems.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration Due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• The value of ‘g’ near Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².
 
• It influences the weight of objects and the work required to move them vertically.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• When a body is lifted, its mechanical energy is conserved, transitioning from kinetic energy to potential energy.
 
• Gravitational potential energy plays a key role in systems like pendulums and roller coasters.

questions.question: Ramu is working hard to push a huge rock by applying 1 N force, but the rock does not move at all. The net work done by Ramu is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Work done is defined as the product of the force applied and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• In this scenario, although Ramu is applying a force of 1 N, the rock does not move. This means the displacement is zero.
 
• Since displacement is zero, the work done (W = Force × Displacement) is also zero.
 
• Therefore, the net work done by Ramu is 0 J, as there is no movement of the rock.
 
• Work is only done when there is a displacement in the direction of the applied force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Work:**

 
 
• Work is a measure of energy transfer when a force moves an object over a distance.
 
• The SI unit of work is the Joule (J).
 
 
 
• **Formula for Work:**
 
 
• Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ), where θ is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
 
 
• **Zero Work:**
 
 
• When the displacement of an object is zero, or the force applied is perpendicular to the direction of displacement, the work done is zero.
 
• Examples include holding a heavy object still or pushing against a wall that doesn’t move.
 
 
 
• **Positive and Negative Work:**
 
 
• Work is positive when the force and displacement are in the same direction.
 
• Work is negative when the force and displacement are in opposite directions.

questions.question: As the temperature increases, the kinetic energy of particles of matter ______
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **kinetic energy** of particles is directly proportional to the **temperature** of the matter. As temperature increases, the particles of matter gain more energy and move faster.
 
• Increased temperature leads to an increase in the **vibrational, rotational, and translational motion** of particles, which directly contributes to higher kinetic energy.
 
• This principle is derived from the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, which states that the temperature of a substance is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
• For example, when water is heated, the molecules move faster, transitioning from a liquid to a gaseous state as the temperature increases.
 
• Temperature increases also cause a change of state (solid to liquid, liquid to gas) due to the higher energy levels of particles overcoming their intermolecular forces.
 
• This concept is fundamental in understanding phenomena such as **thermal expansion, phase changes, and heat transfer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Becomes zero**__

 __
 
• The kinetic energy of particles becomes zero only at **absolute zero temperature (0 Kelvin or -273.15°C)**, which is theoretically the lowest possible temperature where all molecular motion ceases.
 
• This concept is based on the laws of thermodynamics and is practically unattainable.
 
 
 
• **Decreases**__
 __
 
• The kinetic energy of particles decreases only when the temperature of a substance is **lowered**.
 
• This happens during processes such as cooling or freezing, where the particles lose energy and move more slowly.
 
 
 
• **Remains the same**__
 
 
• The kinetic energy of particles remains the same only when the temperature of the system is constant, i.e., there is **no heat transfer or energy exchange**.

questions.question: In which of the following conditions is the work done considered negative?

options.text: When the force is in the direction of displacement.
When the force is perpendicular to the direction of displacement.
When the force is opposite to the direction of displacement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When the force is opposite to the direction of displacement**__.

__
 
• Work done is negative when the force applied on an object is opposite to the direction of the object's displacement.
 
• In this scenario, the angle between the force and displacement is 180 degrees, resulting in a negative value for the work done.
 
• Negative work indicates that the force is acting in the opposite direction to the motion, thereby reducing the object's kinetic energy.
 
• Examples of negative work include frictional forces or any form of resistance that opposes the motion of an object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work and Energy Relationship:**

 
 
• Work done on an object results in a change in its energy. Positive work increases energy, while negative work decreases it.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Work:**
 
 
• Work (W) is calculated as the dot product of force (F) and displacement (d), represented as W = F * d * cos(θ).
 
• θ is the angle between the force and the direction of displacement.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Force:**
 
 
• Friction is a force that opposes the motion of an object and does negative work because it acts opposite to the direction of displacement.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion. When negative work is done, kinetic energy decreases.

questions.question: The work done by a person pushing a brick parallel to the ground with a force of 2 N is 3 J. The displacement caused by the force is equal to ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.5 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Work is defined as the **product of the force applied** and the **displacement caused** in the direction of the force.
 
• The formula for work is: **W = F × d**, where **W** is the work done, **F** is the force applied, and **d** is the displacement.
 
• In this problem, the given values are:
 
 
• **Work (W) = 3 J**
 
• **Force (F) = 2 N**
 
 
 
• To find the displacement, rearrange the formula: **d = W / F**.
 
• Substituting the given values:
 
 
• **d = 3 J / 2 N = 1.5 m**
 
 
 
• Thus, the **displacement** caused by the force is **1.5 meters**.
 
• The correct option is **Option 2**__, which corresponds to **1.5 m**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work**__

 __
 
• **Work** is a scalar quantity that has magnitude but no direction.
 
• The unit of work is the **joule (J)**, where **1 joule = 1 newton meter (N·m)**.
 
• Work is only done when the force has a component in the direction of the displacement.
 
 
 
• **Force**__
 __
 
• **Force** is a vector quantity that can change the state of motion of an object.
 
• Its unit is the **newton (N)**, where **1 newton = 1 kg·m/s²**.
 
• Force can act through contact (e.g., friction) or at a distance (e.g., gravity).
 
 
 
• **Displacement**__
 
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity that represents the shortest path between two points.
 
• It is measured in **meters (m)** and considers both magnitude and direction.
 
• Displacement differs from distance, which is a scalar quantity and does not consider direction.

questions.question: Consider an object moving along a straight line, it starts from point A, reaches point B. and then returns to point A. If the distance between A and B is 20 m, then the net displacement of the object is:

• The initial position and the final position are the same (point A), so the displacement is zero.

Thus, despite the object traveling 40 meters in total (20 meters each way), the **net displacement** is 0 meters, because its initial and final positions coincide.

 
• 
 Net Displacement = Final Position - Initial Position

• Initial position = A So, **Net Displacement = 0 m**.

questions.question: A worker lifts a rice bag of 10 kg from the ground and puts it on the truck 2 m above the ground. Calculate the work done by him on the rice bag. (Given, g= 10 ms-2)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**200 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To calculate the **work done**, we use the formula: **Work Done (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d)**.
 
• The **force** exerted by the worker is equal to the weight of the rice bag, which is calculated by: **Force (F) = Mass (m) × Acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• Here, the **mass** (m) of the rice bag is **10 kg**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** (g) is given as **10 ms⁻²**.
 
• So, the force exerted is: **F = 10 kg × 10 ms⁻² = 100 N**.
 
• The **displacement** (d) of the rice bag is **2 meters** (the height at which the bag is lifted).
 
• Therefore, the work done by the worker is: **W = F × d = 100 N × 2 m = 200 J**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **200 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• In physics, **work** is defined as the amount of energy transferred by a force acting through a distance.
 
• The unit of work is the **joule (J)**, which is equivalent to one newton-meter.
 
 
 
• **Force**__
 __
 
• **Force** is a vector quantity that causes an object to accelerate. It is measured in newtons (N).
 
• One newton is defined as the force required to accelerate a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity**__
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** (g) on the surface of the Earth is approximately **9.8 ms⁻²**, but it is often rounded to **10 ms⁻²** for simplicity in calculations.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a moving body of mass 'm' and velocity 'v' is _______.

options.text: directly proportional to its velocity but inversely proportional to its mass
directly proportional to its mass but inversely proportional to its velocity
inversely proportional to its mass and square of its velocity
directly proportional to its mass and square of its velocity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kinetic energy (KE) of a moving body is given by the formula KE = 0.5 * m * v².
 
• KE is directly proportional to the mass (m) of the body.
 
• KE is directly proportional to the square of the velocity (v²) of the body.
 
• Doubling the mass of the body will double its kinetic energy, keeping velocity constant.
 
• Doubling the velocity of the body will quadruple its kinetic energy, keeping mass constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mass (m):** The amount of matter in a body, which directly influences the kinetic energy of the body.
 
• **Velocity (v):** The speed of an object in a particular direction, crucial in determining the kinetic energy as it is squared in the formula.
 
• **Direct Proportionality:** When one quantity increases, the other quantity increases at the same rate. KE is directly proportional to both mass and the square of velocity.
 
• **Energy Conservation:** In a closed system, the total energy remains constant. Kinetic energy can be transformed into other forms of energy but the total energy remains the same.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: The total energy before and after the transformation always remains constant.
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
The total energy before and after the transformation is not constant.
Energy can only be transformed from one form to another.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Energy** states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
 
• The **total energy** in a closed system remains constant before and after any transformation.
 
• When energy changes form, such as from kinetic to potential energy, the overall energy quantity remains unchanged.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because it contradicts the conservation principle by stating that the total energy before and after the transformation is not constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Law of Thermodynamics:**

 
 
• This law is synonymous with the conservation of energy principle.
 
• It states that the total energy of an isolated system is constant; energy can be transformed from one form to another but cannot be created or destroyed.
 
 
 
• **Forms of Energy:**
 
 
• Energy exists in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, electrical, and nuclear energy.
 
• These forms of energy can transform from one type to another but the total energy remains unchanged in a closed system.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transformation:**
 
 
• Examples include a roller coaster converting potential energy to kinetic energy and vice versa, or a battery converting chemical energy to electrical energy.
 
 
 
• **Closed System:**
 
 
• A closed system is one where no energy enters or leaves the system; the total energy within the system remains constant.

questions.question: An electric water heater converts electrical energy into ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**heat energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric water heater converts electrical energy into heat energy, which is used to heat water.
 
• When electric current passes through the heating element in the water heater, it generates heat due to the resistance of the element.
 
• This heat is transferred to the water, raising its temperature to the desired level.
 
• Heat energy is the most efficient form of energy for heating water, ensuring quick and effective temperature rise.
 
• Electric water heaters are widely used due to their efficiency, safety, and ease of use.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heating Element:**

 
 
• The heating element in an electric water heater is typically made of metal, such as copper or stainless steel, which has high electrical resistance.
 
• When electricity flows through the element, it encounters resistance, causing it to heat up and transfer heat to the water.
 
 
 
• **Thermostat:**
 
 
• Most electric water heaters come with a thermostat to control the water temperature.
 
• The thermostat ensures the water is heated to the set temperature and prevents overheating by cutting off the power supply when the desired temperature is reached.
 
 
 
• **Energy Efficiency:**
 
 
• Electric water heaters are known for their high energy efficiency, often converting nearly all the electrical energy into heat energy.
 
• They are more efficient than gas water heaters in terms of energy conversion and heat retention.
 
 
 
• **Safety Features:**
 
 
• Modern electric water heaters are equipped with safety features like thermal cut-off, pressure relief valves, and automatic shut-off to prevent accidents and ensure safe operation.
